From 4b5d099e1049909a16e93648d80df18a516afb73 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jonathan McPherson <jonathan@rstudio.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Dec 2017 14:58:50 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] save console process before computing interaction mode; fixes
 #1810

this change fixes an issue; because getInteractionMode()
uses the saved console process, it needs to be set before we check the
interaction mode.

diff --git a/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java b/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java
index dbedddd688..0e5b0af8e6 100644
--- a/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java
+++ b/src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java
@@ -76,6 +76,9 @@ public class ConsoleProgressDialog extends ProgressDialog
          throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                "Invalid combination of arguments to ConsoleProgressDialog");
       }
+
+      // save console process so that we can compute interaction mode below
+      consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;
       
       if (getInteractionMode() != ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER)
       {
-- 
2.48.1

## Summary

**File modified:** `src/gwt/src/org/rstudio/studio/client/workbench/views/vcs/common/ConsoleProgressDialog.java`

**Modification:** In the `ConsoleProgressDialog` constructor, the assignment `consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;` was moved earlier in the code, placing it immediately before the call to `getInteractionMode()`. Previously, this field assignment likely occurred after the interaction mode check, causing `getInteractionMode()` to operate on a stale or null `consoleProcess_` value.

**Relationship:** This is a single-file, single-method fix. The `getInteractionMode()` method depends on the `consoleProcess_` instance field to determine the correct interaction mode (e.g., checking against `ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER`). The bug occurred because the field was being read by `getInteractionMode()` before it was properly set with the `consoleProcess` parameter passed into the constructor. By reordering the code so that `consoleProcess_` is assigned **before** the interaction mode check, the method now correctly evaluates the interaction mode based on the actual console process, fixing issue #1810 where incorrect behavior resulted from using an outdated/uninitialized console process reference.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`if (getInteractionMode() != ConsoleProcessInfo.INTERACTION_NEVER)`
`attachToProcess(consoleProcess);`
Reason: `getInteractionMode()` is called before `consoleProcess_` is assigned the incoming `consoleProcess` parameter (the assignment only happens later, indirectly, as part of `attachToProcess`). Since `getInteractionMode()` reads from the instance field `consoleProcess_` rather than the constructor parameter, it operates on a null/stale reference at the time of the call, causing the interaction mode to be computed incorrectly.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`consoleProcess_ = consoleProcess;`
Reason: By explicitly assigning the constructor parameter `consoleProcess` to the instance field `consoleProcess_` before calling `getInteractionMode()`, the method now has access to the correct, up-to-date console process reference when determining the interaction mode, ensuring the mode is computed accurately based on the actual process passed into the constructor.
